Good morning! **Andrew** here, on what should be a big day in Washington, DC.
We'll find out how many US senators are OK with our mad-king president waging
a new US war in the Middle East based, again, on lies. (Surely, only a few,
right? _Right??_)

In today's '**First Draft** ,' Trump could expand his **war on Iran** if
Congress doesn't stop him first, **James Talarico** defeats **Jasmine
Crockett** in the Texas Senate Democratic primary, and **Gavin Newsom**
(_Gavin Newsom!_) suggests Israel is an **" apartheid state." **(Yes, you read
that correctly.)

# **' A Multi-Trillion-Dollar Open-Ended Conflict'**

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!1ZDK!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-
post-

woman on a rooftop as smoke rises in the distance over Tehran following
explosions in the city, on March 3, 2026. Photo by Getty Images._

Over the next two days, we'll find out whether lawmakers in Washington are
ready to fulfill their duties and serve as a check on Donald Trump's
lawlessness, or whether the GOP-led Congress can still rally its narrow
majorities to rubber-stamp the whims of an increasingly fascist and vicious
leader.

Democrats have largely united behind War Powers resolutions in the House and
Senate to block further US military action in Iran without congressional
authorization. The Senate is expected to vote on Wednesday, and the House on
Thursday. These votes are important tests. Unfortunately, Congress will likely
fail them.

While Trump's Iran conflict is the exact type of disastrous regime-change war
that the president and his top officials have all rightfully (disingenuously)
railed against, now that they're in one, they want to ramp it up considerably.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

**" I'm more convinced now that this is going to be open-ended and forever,"**
Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) told reporters after senators received a
classified briefing on the war Tuesday, [according to
HuffPost](https://www.huffpost.com/entry/democrats-raise-alarms-trump-iran-
war_n_69a75d90e4b0c9c664ada332?origin=top-ad-recirc). **" This feels like a
multi-trillion-dollar open-ended conflict with a very confusing and constantly
shifting set of goals."**

Murphy suggested the Trump administration would be **" fine with hard-line
elements being in control"** in Iran, and is in fact already planning to **"
permanently run air operations in order to chase [Iran's] missile-making
capability, drone-making capability, and nuclear capabilities."**

Trump's Iran war doesn't have much support from the American public so far,
[early](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/just-one-four-americans-support-us-
strikes-iran-reutersipsos-poll-finds-2026-03-01/)
[polling](https://criticalissues.umd.edu/feature/do-americans-favor-attacking-
iran-under-current-circumstances-latest-critical-issues-poll-0) shows.
Washington's a unique place, though. Many lawmakers on both sides of the aisle
- and in the Beltway media - are used to backing Israel's interests no matter
what and have no qualms about the idea of bombing countries at will.

Take Republican Senator Josh Hawley (Mo.), who
[described](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/03/lawmakers-trump-
emergency-funding-iran-00810885) the US war on Iran to _Politico_ as **" a
massive operation"** that's **" rapidly changing."** Echoing Murphy, Hawley
said, **" It sounded very open-ended to me."** But Hawley said he'll oppose
the War Powers resolution and allow Trump to keep his war going for now.

He suggested it was fine for Trump to avoid getting congressional
authorization for what he's done so far.

**" If there's not a use of ground troops involved, the president has 60 days
to conduct operations,"** Hawley
[said](https://www.semissourian.com/stories/missouris-josh-hawley-defends-
trumps-iran-strike-rejects-war-powers-vote-de7ef26b/) Tuesday, referring to
the 1973 War Powers Act.

As Rep. Jason Crow (D-Colo.), a member of the House Intelligence Committee,
[pointed out](https://x.com/Acyn/status/2028572294361358564) on Fox a day
earlier, the president only has 60 days to conduct military operations in the
case of an **" imminent threat,"** and Iran did not pose one.

Despite that lack of imminent threat, six pro-Israel Dems have banded together
in the House to [offer a counter-measure](https://www.politico.com/live-
updates/2026/03/03/congress/dems-new-war-powers-measure-00810200) to the War
Powers resolution that could further undermine its prospects for passage: a
separate resolution that would give Trump 30 days to continue his war.

Meanwhile, Trump and his administration can't even keep their pro-war lies
straight - providing fake and shifting rationales for launching their attack
on Iran.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio [gave us some
candor](https://zeteo.com/p/first-draft-trump-iran-marco-rubio-israel) Monday
when he told Capitol Hill reporters that the US had to act against Iran
because **" we knew that there was going to be an Israeli action, we knew that
that would precipitate an attack against American forces."**

Trump rejected this on Tuesday,
[telling](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2028876774407311797) reporters Israel
didn't pull the US into war. **" No, I might have forced their hand. You see,
we were having negotiations with these lunatics, and it was my opinion that
they were going to attack first,"** he said.

A panicky Rubio then tried to walk back his comments to match his boss's
interpretation in another awkward Hill press moment.

When a journalist noted that Rubio said Israel was going to attack Iran and
that's why we needed to get involved, the secretary of state
[replied](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2028930058795049349): **" Your
statement's false." **He continued, **" I was asked very specifically - were
you there yesterday?" **In a rather hilarious moment,**** the reporter
explained that she had been there, and had _asked_ the question.

Rubio continued: **" OK. No, did - were you the one that - because somebody
asked me a question yesterday - did we go in because of Israel? You asked me
that, that follow-up. And I said no. I told you this had to happen anyway. The
president made a decision."**

He was lying, of course, but the idea that the president can so carelessly
decide to launch a war, while his secretary of state flounders on a daily
basis, is a rather large problem for our system of government and a clear
violation of Article I, Section 8, Clause 11 of the Constitution.

The bigger question is: Will a supine, GOP-dominated Congress recognize that
problem and _act_?

## **🇮 🇷 **Iran War Updates

  * **Death tolls:** The death toll in Iran from US-Israeli strikes has climbed to [1,045 people](https://www.reuters.com/world/iran-war-live-israeli-strike-kills-four-lebanon-us-names-its-first-casualties-2026-03-04/), Reuters reported, citing Iranian state media. Dozens of people have been killed by Israel in Lebanon, as the Israeli military continues to bomb and advance further into the country. Six US troops have been killed since the war began, per US Central Command (the Pentagon [identified](https://www.war.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/4420475/dow-identifies-army-casualties/) four of the soldiers yesterday). And 11 people have been killed in Israel. 

  * **Turkey says NATO intercepted missile:** Turkey [said](https://apnews.com/live/iran-war-israel-trump-lebanon-march-04-2026#0000019c-b8b2-d710-adde-fdb706990000) today that NATO had intercepted an Iranian ballistic missile headed towards the country. An attack on Turkey, a NATO member, would mark another major escalation in the war. Iran today [warned](https://apnews.com/live/iran-war-israel-trump-lebanon-march-04-2026#0000019c-b8ba-dfc5-adbd-bdbf32fb0000) that this war could come at the cost of the "complete destruction of the region's military and economic infrastructure."

  * **Strike near US consulate in Dubai** : A small fire broke out near the US consulate in Dubai after an Iranian drone [reportedly](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/03/dubai-us-consulate-fire-drone-strike) hit the parking lot, though no injuries or casualties were reported.****

  * **Internet blackout:** Iran has now been under a near-total, government-imposed communications blackout for more than 100 hours, the internet-access advocacy group Netblocks [said](https://x.com/netblocks/status/2029153937308123202) today.

  * **Who does the US want to lead Iran?:** It's still not clear who exactly the US wants to see lead Iran after its illegal regime change war, with Trump [admitting](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/03/03/world/iran-war-israel-lebanon-trump/e19c431e-7f89-53f2-91c0-87cd59b63eb0?smid=url-share) yesterday that many of the individuals his administration had identified (and their back-up options) have been killed. "I guess the worst case would be we do this, and then somebody takes over who's as bad as the previous person, right," he added. "That could happen."

  * **Supreme leader frontrunner:** Mojtaba Khamenei, the son of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has emerged as the frontrunner to replace the supreme leader, per the _[New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/03/world/middleeast/iran-mojtaba-khamenei-successor.html), _which cited three unnamed Iranian sources.**** Israel's defense minister has [said](https://apnews.com/live/iran-war-israel-trump-lebanon-march-04-2026#0000019c-b797-dfdf-a9df-bfd7766f0000) that the next supreme leader of Iran will become "a target for elimination."

  * **A wannabe 19th-century imperialist** : Trump [said](https://x.com/Acyn/status/2028879038954226090) yesterday that he directed his admin to "cut off all dealings" with Spain after it blocked the US from using jointly-operated bases in the country to attack Iran. He also ludicrously said, "We can use their bases if we want, we can just fly in and use them," he [said](https://x.com/mehdirhasan/status/2028885517782147151). "No one's going to tell us not to use them."

  * **Iranian ship sinks:** Rescue efforts are underway after an Iranian warship sank off the coast of Sri Lanka. Dozens have been rescued from the sinking ship, though more than 100 remain missing. Several bodies have also been recovered, per [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sri-lanka-rescues-30-people-board-distressed-iranian-ship-foreign-minister-says-2026-03-04/).

## 👀 Newsom Says 'Apartheid'

  
[Asked](https://x.com/yashar/status/2029104738818789739) by 'Pod Save America'
co-host **Tommy Vietor** whether the US should "rethink" the US relationship
with Israel, including "military support," California Governor and 2028
Democratic presidential frontrunner **Gavin Newsom** said Netanyahu is **"
trying to stay out of jail. He's got an election coming up. He's potentially
on the ropes. He's got folks, the hard line, that want to annex the West
Bank,"** Newsom said at an event in California last night, adding that some
**" are talking about it appropriately as sort of an apartheid state."**

The times they are a-changin'.

## **🗞 ️ **What You Need to Know

  * **Texas Senate Primary** : State Rep. James Talarico is [projected](https://www.cnn.com/2026/03/04/politics/james-talarico-texas-senate-primary) to win the Texas Senate race and will be the party's Democratic nominee. The Republican candidates - Senator John Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton - will head to a run-off. Could the charismatic Talarico flip the Lone Star State blue in November?

  * **North Carolina House Primary:** In North Carolina's 4th District, Democratic Rep. Valerie Foushee appears to have narrowly, [oh so ](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/us/elections/results-north-carolina-us-house-4-primary.html)_[narrowly](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/us/elections/results-north-carolina-us-house-4-primary.html)_ , fended off a challenge from progressive, pro-Palestine challenger Nida Allam, though the race could be heading to a recount. Foushee benefited from big spending by super PACs tied to the [AI industry](https://prospect.org/2026/02/25/ai-anthropic-claude-super-pac-valerie-foushee-congress-north-carolina/) and [AIPAC](https://readsludge.com/2026/02/26/aipac-donor-tied-group-drops-six-figures-for-foushee-2/). 

  * **Noem in the hot seat** : Homeland Secretary Kristi Noem came under fire from both sides of the aisle during her [testimony](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/3-major-takeaways-from-noems-first-oversight-hearing-since-minneapolis-deaths) before the Senate Judiciary Committee. "What we've seen is a disaster under your leadership, Ms. Noem," GOP Senator Thom Tillis [said](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2028890735152451766?s=46&t=uXB-axTQSod3D2EIebJYlQ), as he [pledged](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/gop-senator-compares-kristi-noems-dhs-leadership-time-shot-dog-rcna261550) to block Trump's nominees and highlighted the department's repeated [efforts](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/03/dhs-noem-obstruction-00810919) to obstruct investigations by its inspector general.

  * **Lutnick to testify** : Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reportedly agreed to a closed-door interview with the House Oversight Committee to discuss his past relations with Jeffrey Epstein, per [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/03/03/lutnick-epstein-files-testify-house?utm_medium=owned_social&utm_campaign=editorial&utm_source=x). Lutnick has been [facing](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/feb/27/howard-lutnick-jeffrey-epstein-photo) growing pressure to testify after documents in the Epstein files showed he and Epstein had multiple interactions, well after he falsely claimed he had stopped associating with the convicted sex offender.

  * **Flip-flop:** Trump's Justice Department abruptly [changed course](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/03/trump-justice-department-law-firms-00809639) and told an appeals court it will continue defending the president's efforts to punish law firms via unconstitutional executive orders - just a day after it told the court it was dropping its appeal.

## 🌏 Anywhere But America

  * **🇵 🇸Don't forget Gaza: **Facing pressure, Israel [reopened](https://www.haaretz.com/gaza/2026-03-04/ty-article/.premium/israel-opens-one-gaza-crossing-for-humanitarian-aid-after-u-s-pressure/0000019c-b7c8-df64-a59c-fffeca8a0000) the Kerem Shalom crossing to allow for the flow of some aid. The aid allowed in, however, is still not even close to the amount Gaza needs, as fears grow over shortages of food and other basic supplies. All other crossings remained closed. 

  * **🇦 🇫 UN issues dire warning: **The UN food program [warned](https://www.ungeneva.org/es/news-media/press-briefing/2026/03/un-geneva-press-briefing) yesterday that 3.7 million children in Afghanistan are expected to suffer from malnutrition this year - 200,000 more than last year - due in part to foreign aid cuts and renewed fighting along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border.

  * **🇸 🇩🇪🇹 Sudan calls out Ethiopia: **Sudan, for the first time since the start of the now three-year civil war, accused Ethiopia of allowing the Rapid Support Forces paramilitary to launch drones from its territory, per [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/sudan-accuses-ethiopia-first-time-involvement-its-civil-war-2026-03-03/).

  * 🇸🇸 **MSF doctors missing:** Doctors Without Borders [said](https://www.doctorswithoutborders.org/what-we-do/where-we-work/south-sudan) this week that 26 local staff members are still unaccounted for, a month after two of its facilities were attacked in South Sudan's Jonglei state amid intense fighting between government and opposition forces.

lethal](https://www.thirdway.org/memo/democrats-abolish-ice-abuses-not-
ice#:~:text=overreach%2C%20and%20fear.-,Abolish%20ICE:%20Emotionally%20Satisfying%2C%20Politically%20Lethal,ICE%20follow%20the%20same%20script.)'.
The good news is it's actually become a pretty popular policy. Even one in
four Republicans supports getting rid of the rogue, masked agency! (See the
